summary: The service started this run, not an instruction. It was triggered when the width-200 baseline loop at f* 0.74 ended (job 164686, unmodified engine with friction). There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. No time went to unasked work. I checked the run's numbers against the raw outputs. All fifty-three per-step entries for the new loop in evidence/E0076-interim.json match the mirrored summary.json files: SHA-256, Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow stretches, with zero mismatches. The loop's range reproduces: Gamma 2.25 to 4.0, fifty-one completed steps. So do both stops. The floor was a CPU cap stop at 2.2, after twenty-three of twenty-five cycles and 2.021 CPU-hours against a two CPU-hour cap. The top was a sphere overlap at 4.05 with cycles_completed 24, so the overlap came in the twenty-fifth cycle, as the run now counts correctly. The step sum (59.61 CPU-hours, against 59.97 in the job record) and the median 25-cycle step (0.862) also match. No step gained energy, failed the audit or slowed down, so the referee check on slow_episodes is clean. I fetched the width-100 ramp.jsonl for f* 0.74. Its SHA-256 matches, and so do its stops: a CPU cap stop at 2.1 on the 0.5 CPU-hour cap, and at 4.15 on the 2.0 cap after completing 4.05 and 4.1. So 'the floor is not comparable, the top is one-sided' is right. The 4.0 step at width 200 did cost 6.23 CPU-hours, about ten times its neighbours, as stated. All three challenges from my previous review were answered. (1) The up-leg cost ratio is now recorded. I recomputed all five f* from the A0068 ramp.jsonl files, whose SHA-256 all match, and the run's 94 ratios came out identical, with an overall median of 7.33. The down-leg table, now with f* 0.74, reproduces with sixty-four pairs and a median of 7.4. The line state now says 'on the way down'. (2) The cycle counting is fixed. (3) The budget figure with the three ended jobs, about 735 of 10000 CPU-hours (7 percent), is given. I have one substantive point and two small ones. (1) The run reads the up-leg medians of about 11.5 at f* 0.44 and 0.57 as width-200 steps being dearer, and from them proposes up-leg caps of '15 or more' CPU-hours. That reading is not what the data show. At both f*, the width-200 step cost stays smooth through Gamma 3.2 to 3.5 (0.99 to 0.84 and 0.86 to 0.74 CPU-hours). The width-100 cost instead halves between 3.3 and 3.4 (0.145 to 0.076 at f* 0.44, 0.137 to 0.066 at f* 0.57) and stays low. The doubled ratio therefore comes from the narrow box changing state, probably to a cheaper pattern, which the wide box does not do in that range. It is not a cost-scaling fact about width 200. Two things follow. No width-200 top so far has been a cap stop, and width-200 up-leg steps cost 0.6 to 1.0 CPU-hours, so their eight CPU-hour cap is far off. The f* 0.74 step at 4.0 used 6.2 of its 8, the closest any has come. So the sentence 'Step caps scaled four times from width 100 are too low on both legs' is shown only for the down leg. For the up leg it is a guess, and proposed direction two should not size caps from the 11.5 medians. The cost drop at width 100 near Gamma 3.35 may also be a box-size difference in its own right, which is what this line is asking about. It is worth one sentence in the E0076 outcome table, checked against the width-100 fields if they were recorded. (2) The f* 0.57 up-leg median is 11.35, so '11.5 at f* 0.44 and 0.57' in the headline, note, PROGRAM.md and progress.md should read 11.5 and 11.4. (3) The L0018 note and update in ledger/lines.jsonl carry the time 18:28:00Z. That is after the run's commit at 18:24:29Z, after its own recorded end at 18:25:30Z, and after I started this review at 18:26. Timestamps written ahead had been fixed in the second run and are back. The run discloses this itself. The line state holds otherwise: twenty of thirty loops running, ten ended (one E0075 and nine E0076 job records), and five baseline loops finished. program check passes. It lists one approval in the last day (approved/20261124T031934297997Z, Nov 24 03:19), which I reported before; whether it was Chris's is for Chris to confirm. sequel-data is 650 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling, and free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. active.jsonl is empty. tmp/ held only my own fetch of five ramp.jsonl files, which I deleted. Outside the two allowed folders, nothing was written in the run's window except the harness's own ~/.claude.json. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was an eight-minute service run. The job record was committed at 18:17:16, and the run says it started at 18:18:22. Its two commits are at 18:24:29 and 18:24:49, and its recorded end is 18:25:30. It only read fetched outputs, so the zero local CPU-hours it recorded is right. Twenty of thirty width-200 loops are still running on Hatteras: ten E0074, nine E0075 and one E0076 (f* 0.38, job 164691). None was started, cancelled or restarted. active.jsonl is empty, which is correct for cluster jobs. The host is a Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be measured, and the summary says so. Free disk was 91 gigabytes, as recorded. The machine did not limit the science. The loops' own CPU caps set the floors, and the run says so.
discrepancies: scheduled_start (18:17:09Z) is the job's end time, not a measured runner start, as the summary itself admits.
The ledger/lines.jsonl note and update for L0018 are stamped 18:28:00Z, later than the run's last commit (18:24:49Z) and its recorded end (18:25:30Z).
